newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank cuts overnight rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank cuts overnight rates.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank on Monday said it had cut its overnight borrowing rate to 11.00 percent from 12.50 percent and its lending rate to 13.00 percent from 14.50.
The interest rate cut came after the peso-dollar rate showed stability by the end of last week.

The Bank last week raised its overnight rates on two successive days to quell speculation in the peso. The peso ended sharply down to 26.265 to the dollar last Monday from the previous close of 26.211. It ended the week at 26.222.
The Central Bank lifted its overnight borrowing rate to 12.50 percent from 10.25 and its overnight lending rate to 14.50 percent from 12.75.
"Given that the foreign exchange market has stabilised a little bit, the Central Bank has decided to lower its rates and see how the market will react," said a trader from a local bank.
If the market reverts to speculative mood, the Central Bank will probably use interest rates again, the trader said.
The Central Bank kept its term reverse repo rates unchanged on Monday. The one-month bills stayed at 11.250 percent, the two-month at 11.3750 and the three-month at 11.5.
